# The cls convenience family cannot express a swap in one update

## Context

**Framing from @tobiu, and it bounds this ticket: *"it is not crucial, but a convenience method. good for DX and MX."*** This is not a correctness or performance defect — nothing is broken today. It is an API-completeness gap that makes the ergonomic spelling of a common operation cost more than the terse one.

Origin: #15202 prescribed migrating application class transitions onto `removeCls()` / `addCls()`. I implemented it (#18735 + `neomjs/devindex#14`) and @tobiu caught that it **replaces one vdom update with two**. Both PRs are closed and #15202's premise is falsified — the aggregate read-mutate-assign is the engine's own intended idiom, made safe by `beforeGetCls` returning `[...value]`. This ticket is the one real thing that lane surfaced.

## The Problem

`component.Base`'s class helpers are each `get-copy → mutate → assign`:

```js
addCls(value)           { let {cls} = this; NeoArray.add(cls, value);            this.cls = cls }
removeCls(value)        { let  cls  = this.cls; NeoArray.remove(cls, value);     this.cls = cls }
toggleCls(value, add)   { let  cls  = this.cls; NeoArray.toggle(cls, value, add); this.cls = cls }
```

`afterSetCls` ends in `me.update()`, and the in-flight guard **defers rather than merges** — `needsVdomUpdate = true` at `mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:1090`, re-fired at `:403`. Per the batching model the first config change takes a worker round trip and the rest batch into a second, so composing two helpers costs **2 round trips** where one assignment costs 1.

The family is symmetric except for one hole:

| layer | add | remove | toggle | **swap** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `util/Array` | `add` | `remove` | `toggle` | **`removeAdd`** ✅ |
| `component.Base` | `addCls` | `removeCls` | `toggleCls` | **— missing** ❌ |

**A swap is the one operation the family cannot express.** The compositional test — *can a caller build this from existing members at the same cost?* — is yes for add/remove/toggle and **no** for swap. `removeAdd` exists one layer down; the lift to the component layer was never made, so callers either hand-roll it or pay the extra round trip.

## The Architectural Reality

The engine has **two** established idioms, and only the first is in scope:

1. **One-shot swap** — `component/Icon.mjs:41`:
   ```js
   let cls = this.cls;
   NeoArray.removeAdd(cls, oldValue, value);
   this.cls = cls
   ```
2. **Swap plus further config changes** — `tab/Container.mjs:251`:
   ```js
   NeoArray.remove(cls, 'neo-' + oldValue);
   NeoArray.add(cls, 'neo-' + value);
   me.setSilent({cls});          // more configs follow; one flush
   ```

Form 2 is already correct and must not be touched — `set()` / `setSilent()` / the `silentVdomUpdate` bracket (`toolbar/Breadcrumb.mjs:198-229`, `form/field/Text.mjs:783-791`) are the right tool when cls changes alongside other configs, and `removeAddCls` would not improve them.

`NeoArray.remove` and `.add` both accept an item **or an array**, so the signature must pass through: `grid/header/Button.mjs:133` removes **two** classes and adds one.

## The Fix

Add one method to `src/component/Base.mjs`, beside `addCls` / `removeCls` / `toggleCls`:

```js
removeAddCls(removeItems, addItems) {
    let cls = this.cls;

    NeoArray.removeAdd(cls, removeItems, addItems);
    this.cls = cls
}
```

One assignment, one round trip, arrays accepted on both sides. Then migrate the **one-shot `this.cls` swap** sites to it.

**Enumerated candidates** (from a `remove`→`add`-pair sweep across `src` + `apps`). Every one needs per-site confirmation at implementation time — the sweep classifies by what the local `cls` variable points at, which is exactly the check I got wrong twice in the originating lane:

| servable — `this.cls`, one-shot | |
|---|---|
| `component/Icon.mjs:41` | already `removeAdd`; collapses to one line |
| `button/Base.mjs:330` · `component/StatusBadge.mjs:298` · `form/field/FileUpload.mjs:775` | confirm each |
| `grid/header/Button.mjs:133,139` · `table/header/Button.mjs:136,141` | multi-remove + single add |
| `form/field/CheckBox.mjs:333` | confirm |
| `apps/portal/view/Viewport.mjs` · `apps/shareddialog/view/MainContainerController.mjs` | app sites |

| **excluded** | why |
|---|---|
| `tab/Container.mjs:251` | uses `setSilent({cls})` — already one flush |
| ⚠️ **`component/IconLink.mjs:68`** | **the look-alike trap.** Reads identically to `Icon.mjs:41` at a glance, but `node = me.vdom.cn[0]` — it mutates a **child** node. `removeAddCls` targets the vdomRoot, so migrating this one would be a defect, not a cleanup. Verified by @neo-opus-ada on #18738. |
| `button/Base.mjs:242` · `container/AccordionItem.mjs:141` · `form/field/Text.mjs:544,824` · `form/field/CheckBox.mjs:317` | mutate a **child / label / vdom node** `cls`, not `this.cls` |
| `form/field/CheckBox.mjs:227` | operates on `iconCls` |
| `layout/Card.mjs` | `wrapperCls` / `childCls` |

**Accretion Defense — the deletion is named.** ~8 engine lines added; each migrated site drops from 3 lines to 1, and sites whose only remaining `NeoArray` use was the swap drop the import too. Net consumer-line reduction, and the `*Cls` family becomes complete rather than gaining a special case.

## Decision Record impact

`none`. New public convenience on an existing family, no contract change to `cls`, `afterSetCls`, or the update pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `removeAddCls(removeItems, addItems)` exists on `Neo.component.Base` beside the other `*Cls` helpers, with JSDoc, and performs exactly one `cls` assignment.
- [ ] It accepts an item **or an array** for both arguments, proven by a unit arm covering the multi-remove case (`grid/header/Button.mjs`'s two-remove-one-add shape).
- [ ] A unit arm asserts **one** `update()` per `removeAddCls` call — a round-trip/update **count**, not DOM class state. (See Avoided Traps: a DOM-state assertion passes while the cost doubles.)
- [ ] Every site in the servable table is individually confirmed as `this.cls` + one-shot before migration; any that is not is moved to the excluded table with its reason recorded in the PR.
- [ ] Each migrated site performs the same number of round trips as before — never more.
- [ ] No site in the excluded table is modified.
- [ ] Sites whose last `NeoArray` reference was the swap drop the import; a scoped grep confirms no unused import remains.
- [ ] Rendered behaviour is unchanged at every migrated site — the class set after the transition is identical.

## Out of Scope

- Any migration to `removeCls()` + `addCls()` — that is the retracted #18735 shape and costs an extra round trip.
- `set()` / `setSilent()` / `silentVdomUpdate` call sites, and converting anything **to** them.
- Child-node, label-element, `wrapperCls`, `childCls` and `iconCls` sites.
- `NeoArray.removeAdd` itself, and the `cls` reactive-config contract.
- #15202's premise — falsified, addressed on that ticket.

## Avoided Traps

**A DOM-class-state assertion cannot see this.** In #18735 I shipped a `MutationObserver` spec *with a positive control* proving no intermediate DOM class state, and cited it as licence. The deferred second cycle mutates no classes, so the instrument agreed and **could not have disagreed**. A positive control proves the observer can see what it watches; it says nothing about whether that is the right axis. **AC-3 is therefore written as an update count.**

**Do not trust a `cls`-named local.** A `remove`→`add` pair on a variable called `cls` says nothing about whether it is `this.cls`. In the sweep above, `CheckBox.mjs:227` is `iconCls` and `IconLink.mjs:68` is a child node — I asserted both as servable before checking, and had to correct it. Resolve the assignment for every site.

**Do not extrapolate cost from a guard.** Reading `needsVdomUpdate` tells you a second cycle exists; it does not tell you how many. I claimed N+1 for loop-shaped call sites and was wrong — batching caps it at 2 regardless of iteration count.

- `component/Icon.mjs:41` — the one-shot precedent · `tab/Container.mjs:251` — the `setSilent` precedent.

- 2026-09-15T15:03:08Z @tobiu referenced in commit `1ef29df` - "feat(component): the cls family can express a swap, so callers stop paying a second update for one (#18736) (#18738)

`addCls`, `removeCls` and `toggleCls` each assign `cls`, and `afterSetCls` ends in
`update()`. So a swap — the most common multi-class operation in the engine — could
only be spelled by composing two of them, which costs two vdom updates where one
assignment costs one. `util.Array` has carried `removeAdd` for exactly this; the lift
to the component layer was never made, so six sites hand-rolled it instead.

`removeAddCls(removeItems, addItems)` is that lift: one assignment, one update, single
items or arrays on both sides. The spec counts `update()` calls rather than asserting
the resulting class set, and keeps the composed two-call form as a control that reports
2 — a set assertion cannot tell the forms apart, so a DOM-state witness passes while
the work doubles.

Six sites migrate. The two sort-header switches lose their `{cls}` destructure and their
trailing assignment, and no longer fire an update when `value` matches no case.
`component/Icon.mjs` drops its now-unused `NeoArray` import.

Excluded, with reasons: sites mutating a child, label, wrapper or icon `cls` rather than
`this.cls`; `tab/Container.mjs`, which already batches via `setSilent({cls})`; and
`form/field/FileUpload.mjs`, which combines a swap with an independent toggle — a
combination this method deliberately cannot express, and where the aggregate form
remains correct at one update."
